skill.name: iotnet
skill.description: Analyze IoT network packet captures and live traffic to identify protocols, weak authentication, plaintext credentials, and missing encryption.
skill.summary: Analyze IoT network traffic and highlight protocol security risks.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline option formatting. The confirmed risks are sudo-based live packet capture and sensitive traffic inspection without explicit authorization guardrails. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Live capture uses sudo and root packet access.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of authorization and scope before any live capture. Prefer offline PCAP analysis when possible.

remediation.issue: The skill can expose sensitive packet data.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions to redact credentials, device identifiers, and private addresses before sharing results.
Require users to name the owned network, device, interface, and permitted IP ranges before applying filters.
Document the expected iotnet binary path, required permissions, and safe failure handling for missing tools.

- `-c, --capture-filter`: BPF syntax filter for live capture
- `--display-filter`: Wireshark display filter for PCAP analysis
- `--config`: Custom IoT detection rules configuration file

content.value_statement: IoT traffic can hide insecure protocols, weak authentication, and plaintext credentials. This skill guides PCAP and live-capture analysis with IoTNet and clear remediation summaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides offline analysis of one or more PCAP files with IoTNet.
Guides live capture on a named network interface for a selected duration.
Applies IP, capture, and display filters when the user provides scope.
Identifies IoT protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, Z-Wave, ONVIF, UPnP, and Modbus.
Summarizes vulnerabilities such as plaintext credentials, missing TLS, weak authentication, and insecure protocol versions.
Can request text, JSON, quiet, or verbose output from the tool.
limitations: Live capture requires root privileges and should only run on authorized networks.
It depends on the IoTNet binary and detection rules being installed.
Findings depend on packet capture quality and protocol visibility.
Encrypted traffic may hide application details and credentials.

use_cases.title: Review Lab IoT Traffic
use_cases.description: Analyze captured smart-device traffic to identify protocols, plaintext credentials, and missing encryption before deployment.

use_cases.title: Audit Device Communications
use_cases.description: Inspect PCAP files from managed devices and convert protocol findings into remediation actions for engineering teams.

use_cases.title: Triage Network Evidence
use_cases.description: Summarize suspicious IoT communication patterns from captures during incident response or compliance review.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a PCAP
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this IoT packet capture with IoTNet: [pcap path]. Summarize detected protocols, vulnerabilities, and remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Filter One Device
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [pcap path] for traffic involving [device IP]. Focus on IoT protocols, authentication, encryption, and risky behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Captures
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these captures: [pcap paths]. Compare protocol distribution, repeated vulnerabilities, and device-specific risks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Scoped Live Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: On my authorized lab network, capture [interface] for [duration] with filter [scope]. Report IoT protocols, vulnerabilities, and safe remediation.

output_examples.input: Analyze smart-home-lab.pcap for MQTT security issues.
output: Detected MQTT and SSDP traffic across three IoT devices.
Flagged plaintext MQTT authentication and missing TLS.
Recommended broker authentication, TLS, and network segmentation.

output_examples.input: Review capture files from a managed camera deployment.
output: Found ONVIF, RTSP, SSDP, and vendor update traffic.
Marked unauthenticated discovery responses as medium risk.
Recommended firmware review, access controls, and management VLAN isolation.

output_examples.input: Summarize IoT protocol exposure from a scoped live capture.
output: Captured traffic for the authorized interface and duration.
Identified CoAP and MQTT flows with protocol counts.
Highlighted missing encryption and the devices that need follow-up.

best_practices: Use offline PCAP analysis when live capture is not required.
Confirm authorization and scope before selecting an interface, IP address, or filter.
Redact plaintext credentials and device identifiers before sharing results.
anti_patterns: Running live capture on networks you do not own or administer.
Using broad filters when a narrow protocol, interface, or host scope is available.
Treating automated protocol findings as final without validating packet context.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes IoT network traffic from PCAP files or scoped live captures using IoTNet.

faq.question: Does live capture require elevated privileges?
faq.answer: Yes. Live capture requires root or sudo privileges and should only run on authorized networks.

faq.question: Which protocols can it identify?
faq.answer: It can identify protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, Z-Wave, ONVIF, UPnP, and Modbus.

faq.question: Can it find plaintext credentials?
faq.answer: It can flag plaintext credentials when packet contents expose them and the capture includes the relevant traffic.

faq.question: Can it analyze encrypted traffic?
faq.answer: It can report metadata and protocol presence, but encryption may hide application details and credentials.

faq.question: What should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide PCAP paths or authorized live-capture scope, plus any IP, protocol, or display filters.
